name: The Cyprus crossing

segments.name: The Levantine coast
segments.notes: Working north with the land in sight, past fishing beaches and the last warehouses.

segments.name: Open water
segments.notes: Away from the coast, where the crossing belongs to weather and the master's reading of it.

segments.name: The Cypriot approach
segments.notes: The island rises as a low smudge, then a coast of pale rock and drawn-up boats.

waypoints.name: A quiet anchorage
waypoints.description: A shallow bay where the boat waits out the dark and nobody is in a hurry.

waypoints.name: A harbor check
waypoints.description: A small harbor where a clerk takes an interest in cargo he did not load.

modes.name: Coastal
modes.description: Hug the shore, anchor at night. Slower, cheaper, and the captain knows where the water is shallow.

modes.name: Open water
modes.description: Straight across. Fewer nights, more weather, and no land to run for.

requirementsNote: No master will take you without a word in Akkadian or a captain who knows your face.
closureNote: The harbor is closed to departures.

sources: Late Bronze Age eastern Mediterranean maritime exchange, general
provenance.notes: A sea crossing between the Levantine coast and Cyprus is plausible and well attested in general terms. The specific route, timings, and fares are game abstraction.
